name: Nu Holdings
thesis: Latin America's leading digital bank (Brazil + Mexico + Colombia), where the thesis is fundamentally about generating exceptional ROE — the top-of-list monitorable, tracked for trend over time with any sustained dip below 25% a thesis-level warning — driven by expanding risk-adjusted net interest margin (NIM minus cost of risk), which sits alongside ROE as the second top-of-list monitorable because it is the precursor that feeds the ROE math, while maintaining a prudent capital cushion and demonstrating tight command of seasonal NPL ratios per product × geography. Below those two headline gauges, the product × country penetration/credit matrix remains the central operating monitorable: Brazil credit card penetration approaching saturation while personal loans and secured lending remain underpenetrated, Mexico deposit-led acquisition outpacing credit ramp, Colombia still in land-grab. Three engines feed the ROE math: (1) in Brazil, customer count is now a secondary monitorable — the maturing base means growth flows through ARPAC and credit mix rather than net adds, while customer compounding remains the primary engine in Mexico/Colombia where low-CAC acquisition on network effects is still doing the heavy lifting, (2) ARPAC ramping as customers add credit + investment products and as funding mix shifts toward low-cost deposits — the slope differs sharply by country cohort and product mix, lifting risk-adjusted NIM, and is the dominant Brazil lever from here, (3) operating leverage as cost-to-serve stays near-zero. Bet: 25%+ revenue growth with ROE crossing 30% and trending durably above the 25% floor, sustained by risk-adjusted NIM expansion that more than absorbs seasonal NPL formation (Brazilian unsecured cycles peak Q1–Q2; Mexico's young book has yet to season) while CET1 stays comfortably above regulatory floors. Durable Brazil profitability — now monetization-led, not acquisition-led — funds Mexico/Colombia expansion only if credit exposure ramps are paced against NPL formation per product per geography, and only if growth-market customer adds keep compounding to seed the future ARPAC base. An ROE trend breaking below 25% on a sustained basis (the headline thesis-killer), risk-adjusted NIM compression from funding-cost shocks or unprovisioned loss migration (the precursor signal that typically arrives before the ROE break), a Brazil credit-card NPL break (tracked as a consolidated NPL indicator spanning the 15–90 day early-bucket and 90+ day late-bucket cohorts, evaluated on a YoY change basis at the same quarter-end rather than against a static threshold so the signal flexes with the underwriting-mix profile and neutralizes the Q1–Q2 seasonal peak — a material YoY deterioration versus the prior-year comparable quarter is the trigger), a Brazil ARPAC stall as the base matures, a Mexico/Colombia customer-acquisition slowdown that starves the next leg, a Mexico unsecured-credit ramp outrunning underwriting capacity, capital ratios drawn down to fund growth without commensurate earnings power, or a single-quarter YoY revenue growth rate decelerating by more than 80% versus the prior-year comparable (i.e., the YoY growth print collapsing to under one-fifth of the preceding year's pace) are what kill the thesis.
key_driver: Customer count × ARPAC × NIM with NPL controlled

tier_1_kpis.name: Return on equity (ROE)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Sustained dip below 25% (2 consecutive Qs) — top-of-list monitorable, tracked for trend over time

tier_1_kpis.name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Risk-adjusted NIM compresses >100bps YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (precursor that feeds the ROE math)

tier_1_kpis.name: Total customers (millions)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Net adds <5M per quarter for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: Monthly ARPAC (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: ARPAC growth <15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: NPL total ratio (15-90d + 90d+) YoY change
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Consolidated NPL ratio rises >150bps YoY (same-quarter PY comparison to neutralize seasonality) for 2 consecutive Qs

thesis_breakers_qualitative: ROE sustained below 25% (top-of-list monitorable — franchise economics deteriorating)
Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk) compresses on sustained basis — precursor that feeds the ROE math
Consolidated NPL (15-90d + 90d+) rises >150bps YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (seasonality-adjusted credit-cycle break)

break_rules.narrative: ROE dips below 25% for 2 consecutive Qs. ROE is the top-of-list monitorable for NU — the entire thesis hinges on generating exceptional ROE, so a sustained dip below 25% is a thesis-level warning that the franchise economics are deteriorating.

break_rules.kpi_name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
break_rules.narrative: Risk-adjusted NIM compresses by more than 100bps YoY for 2 consecutive Qs. Risk-adjusted NIM is the precursor that feeds the ROE math — sustained compression here mechanically pulls ROE down and is the second top-of-list monitorable alongside ROE itself.
Revenue YoY growth rate decelerates by more than 80% quarter-over-quarter (e.g., 40% YoY → 8% YoY).

Consolidated NPL ratio (15-90d plus 90d+) rises more than 1.5 percentage points (150bps) versus the same quarter prior year for 2 consecutive Qs. Same-quarter YoY comparison neutralizes seasonality and lets the threshold travel with the underwriting mix (e.g., riskier secured/unsecured blend) rather than enforcing a static absolute level.

business_model_rules.narrative: 90d+ NPL > 7% for 2Q — credit-quality break; their underwriting thesis depends on the 5-6% historical range holding.
Monthly ARPAC < $10 for 2Q — cross-sell stalling; expanding ARPAC is the unit-economics flywheel.
Activity rate < 82% for 2Q — customers becoming dormant; engagement-flywheel signal.
15-90d NPL > 5% for 2Q — leading indicator of cohort credit deterioration; fires 1-2Q before 90d+ trips.
